newsitem.title: INDIA: India IOC says cannot borrow more-paper.
newsitem.headline: India IOC says cannot borrow more-paper.

text.p: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) has told the government it has exhausted its enhanced $3.5 billion external commercial borrowing (ECB) limit, the Business Standard newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The state-run firm, which has a monopoly over crude oil imports, told the government it would not be able to raise further loans in the international market as its debt to equity ratio has touched two to one, the newspaper said.

"IOC ... has cautioned that under the present circumstances it would be difficult for it to continue uninterrupted imports of petroleum products which may lead to serious disruption in supplies," it said.
IOC called for immediate steps to tackle the oil pool account deficit which touched 155 billion rupees on March 31, Business Standard said.
The oil pool deficit represents money owed by the government to oil companies for selling below market prices to support India's complex petroleum products cross-subsidy system.

"IOC has written to both the finance and the petroleum ministries that it is only a matter of time before domestic refineries, which are not getting their dues from the oil coordination committee that manages the oil pool account, start closing down gradually because of their inability to pay for their supplies of crude oil," it added.

"IOC is learnt to have informed the government that the $500 million raised by it recently in Singapore could be the last foreign loan arranged by it under the current difficult oil pool position," the paper said.
"Foreign banks may not risk their capital till the oil pool situation improves," it said.
